newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: India offers to help end Sri Lanka war.
newsitem.headline: India offers to help end Sri Lanka war.

text.p: India, which 10 years ago sent troops to Sri Lanka in an abortive bid to end the island's protracted separatist war, said on Wednesday it would do anything it could to help bring the conflict to a close.
"India is ready to provide Sri Lanka any help she could give," External Affairs Minister Inder Kumar Gujral told a news conference.
He said India supported a peaceful settlement of the conflict, now in its 14th year. "We are committed to a policy of good neighbourliness and non-interference in Sri Lanka's affairs," he said.

Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar said Colombo had not asked for military aid from India to fight the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas, but that the continued dialogue marked improved ties between the neighbours.
"This meeting has marked an historic and almost dramatic enhancement of relations between the two countries," Kadirgamar told the news conference at the end of Gujral's four-day visit.

India sent troops to Sri Lanka under a 1987 peace pact to try to end the fighting between the rebels and Sri Lankan security forces. The Indian troops were withdrawn in 1990 after an inconclusive campaign.
Kadirgamar said the two countries and the provincial government of Tamil Nadu in southern India would maintain close co-operation and dialogue to sort out any problems.
Sri Lankan Tamil separatist groups ran safe havens in Tamil Nadu during the early stages of their struggle in the 1980s.
Kadirgamar also accused the rebels of trying to disrupt ties between Colombo and New Delhi with the reported killing of an Indian fisherman on Tuesday in the Palk Strait dividing the two countries.
"This area is a well-known route for the LTTE," Kadirgamar said. "This incident is a deliberate LTTE effort to disrupt Indo-Lanka relations, especially during (Gujral's visit)."
Separately, Gujral said India would soon remove quotas and cut tariffs on 70 to 80 Sri Lankan exports.

Colombo has been trying to get India to remove quantitative restrictions on exports, especially agricultural products like rubber, cloves and cinnamon, and consumer goods such as ceramics and confectionery.
Gujral arrived on the island on Sunday to co-chair with Kadirgamar the India-Sri Lanka Joint Commission, which was set up in 1991 to foster co-operation. It last met in April 1994 in New Delhi.
The two countries also signed an investment protection agreement.
Colombo has been urging its giant neighbour to import more goods from Sri Lanka and invest more in the island. Their balance of trade is heavily in India's favour.
Sri Lankan exports to India stood at $30 million in 1995 while Indian exports to Sri Lanka topped $450 million.
